papers.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
papers.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, especially scATAC-seq, are being used to map the epigenetic regulatory programs that control bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration, and how these programs go awry in skeletal diseases. It highlights how these approaches reveal transcription factor binding dynamics and gene regulatory networks at single-cell resolution, providing a framework for understanding bone cell fate and function.

papers.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.
papers.summary: This paper develops a knowledge graph that organizes traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with emotional comorbidities such as anxiety, depression, and insomnia, linking syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs to their sources. It then evaluates the graph's contribution to generated answers through a blinded question-answering assessment, addressing whether structured TCM knowledge improves answer quality beyond raw text generation.

papers.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
papers.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: sacchar
papers.summary: This paper describes how the CABBI research center organized a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn framework to engineer C4 grasses (including sugarcane and sorghum) to accumulate triacylglycerol oil in vegetative biomass rather than just seeds. It highlights the need to coordinate molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program to make vegetative oil production viable for renewable fuels and biobased chemicals. The work serves as a lessons-learned account of how large interdisciplinary bioenergy consortia can structure their research.

papers.title: Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.
papers.abstract: Model organisms carry decades of systematic gene-phenotype annotation, but connecting those annotations to human disease is rarely straightforward. Phenologs offer a principled way to bridge this gap. A human disease and a model-organism phenotype are phenologs when their associated genes, linked by orthology, overlap more than expected by chance, so the genes of one become candidates for the other. Here we compute phenologs from the Monarch Knowledge Graph, which integrates gene-disease, gene-phenotype and orthology data for human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as ort
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors computed phenologs—statistical overlaps between human disease genes and model-organism phenotype genes linked by orthology—at knowledge-graph scale using the Monarch Knowledge Graph, covering human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as orthology units, they produced a catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases, including cross-species links such as mouse-to-slime-mold. This provides a broad, principled resource for prioritizing disease-gene candidates from model-organism annotations.

papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that consolidates literature-derived evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making the evidence reusable and auditable. This resource addresses the fragmentation of spillover evidence across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, and genomic studies.

papers.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.
papers.summary: This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to predict acute kidney injury before onset and to forecast prognosis after diagnosis. The approach addresses the high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity of EHR data that challenge conventional machine learning methods.

papers.title: Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.
papers.abstract: Psychiatric diagnostic practice faces persistent challenges in adequately capturing the complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of mental disorders. Conventional categorical classification systems such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) rely on rigid symptom-based criteria that often fail to represent multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and high rates of comorbidity. Although dimensional models, domain-specific ontologies, and alternative taxonomi
papers.summary: This paper develops a Meta Mesh Ontology designed to integrate mental health knowledge across different domains, addressing the limitations of rigid categorical diagnostic systems like DSM-5 and ICD-11. The ontology aims to better capture the complexity, heterogeneity, and comorbidity of mental disorders by combining dimensional models and domain-specific ontologies. It is evaluated as a tool for cross-domain knowledge integration in psychiatry.

papers.title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell spatial omics (SCSO) has reshaped spatial profiling by enabling simultaneous molecular characterization and spatial mapping at single-cell resolution, providing insights into cellular identities and tissue architecture within native biological contexts. By integrating spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities, SCSO datasets have been widely used to construct spatially resolved cell atlases, characterize disease-associated tissue remodeling, and map disease-relevant cell populations. However, these SCSO datasets remain fragmented across individual publications,
papers.summary: scSpatial is a new atlas/database that consolidates single-cell spatial omics datasets, which were previously scattered across individual publications. It integrates spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities to support construction of spatially resolved cell atlases and mapping of disease-associated tissue remodeling. The resource aims to make SCSO data more accessible and reusable for the spatial omics community.

papers.title: AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance.
papers.abstract: Biomedical artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relies on heterogeneous data sources, yet differences in data structure, terminology, evidence quality, and provenance complicate their integration into reliable knowledge resources. Here, we develop an evidence-aware framework for processing and integrating heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data from FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and electronic health records in Mass General Brigham. The framework combines large language model (LLM)-based information extraction, ontology-driven sem
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present an evidence-aware AI framework that integrates heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data—FAERS reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and EHRs—using LLM-based extraction and ontology-driven semantic harmonization. The work aims to produce a reliable knowledge resource for adverse event discovery despite differences in data structure, terminology, and evidence quality across sources.

papers.title: The Drosophila Secretome.
papers.abstract: Secreted proteins are synthesized within the cell and actively transported outside, where they contribute to development, physiology, immunity, and cell-cell communication. In Drosophila melanogaster , many secreted proteins are evolutionarily conserved, making this species a powerful model for studying human development, cancer, neurobiology, and immune regulation. To assemble the Drosophila secretome, we systematically analyzed all fly protein sequences with computational tools, integrating FlyBase, UniProt and Gene Ontology annotations, and incorporating large-scale proteomics datasets. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes a systematic computational assembly of the Drosophila secretome, integrating FlyBase, UniProt, and Gene Ontology annotations with large-scale proteomics datasets to identify proteins that are actively secreted. The resulting resource catalogs secreted fly proteins, many of which are evolutionarily conserved, providing a foundation for studying development, immunity, cancer, and neurobiology in a model organism.

papers.title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconcep
papers.summary: This review argues that precision nutrition—tailoring dietary recommendations using multi-omics, wearables, and AI/ML—remains difficult to translate into practice because evidence is fragmented across life stages and systems-biology knowledge is poorly integrated. The authors frame nutritional needs and response heterogeneity as dynamic across the lifespan, from preconception onward, and call for better integration of these influences to move the field toward clinical application.

papers.title: Ontology- and Data-Driven Circularity Assessment of Waste-Derived Rigid PVC-u: A Micro-Macro Decision Framework for Sustainable Recycling and Smart Manufacturing.
papers.abstract: The circularity of waste-derived rigid unplasticised poly (vinyl chloride) (PVC-u) is constrained by heterogeneous waste-stream sources, degraded material quality, legacy additives, and inconsistent decision criteria spanning technical, environmental, and economic aspects. In this work, we developed an ontology- and data-driven circularity assessment framework for waste-derived rigid PVC-u recycling systems, built on a Protégé ontology coupled with big data analytics. The framework structures knowledge on materials, recycling processes, process parameters, quality aspects, sustainability measu
papers.summary: This paper develops a framework for assessing the circularity of recycled rigid PVC-u, combining a Protégé-based ontology with big data analytics to organize knowledge about materials, recycling processes, quality, and sustainability. It aims to support decision-making across technical, environmental, and economic dimensions for sustainable recycling and smart manufacturing.

papers.title: WingShape-Warn: A Morphology-Driven Early-Warning Pipeline for Mosquito-Borne Disease Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Environmental stressors-including climate change, urbanisation, and pollution-are increasingly altering the wing morphology of mosquito vectors. These morphological shifts, particularly in wing geometry, can serve as early-warning indicators for mosquito abundance and arboviral disease outbreaks. However, quantitative wing-shape analysis remains underutilised in operational mosquito surveillance and public health early-warning systems. This Technology and Code article presents WingShape-Warn, a reproducible, open-source pipeline that integrates geometric morphometrics, deep learning-based imag
papers.summary: WingShape-Warn is an open-source, reproducible pipeline that combines geometric morphometrics with deep learning-based image analysis to quantify mosquito wing shape from images. The authors propose that wing morphology shifts driven by environmental stressors can act as early-warning indicators of mosquito abundance and arboviral outbreak risk, aiming to bring quantitative wing-shape analysis into operational surveillance. The work is a technology/code contribution rather than a validated field study.

papers.title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Reveals Evolutionary Features of Glugea plecoglossi, a Fish-Infecting Microsporidian Parasite of Ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis).
papers.abstract: Microsporidia are obligate intracellular parasites with extensively reduced genomes, yet substantial genomic variation occurs among lineages. Glugea plecoglossi infects ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis) and forms conspicuous xenomas, but its genome characteristics and evolutionary position remain poorly resolved. We generated a genome assembly of G. plecoglossi and compared it with 42 additional microsporidian taxa using phylogenomics, functional profiling, repeat analysis, and multi-copy orthogroup analysis. The 16.71 Mb assembly comprised 59 scaffolds, with a scaffold N50 of 557.5 kb and 78.5% co
papers.summary: This study presents a genome assembly of Glugea plecoglossi, a microsporidian parasite that infects ayu fish and forms xenomas, and compares it with 42 other microsporidian taxa using phylogenomics and functional profiling. The 16.71 Mb assembly provides new insight into the genomic features and evolutionary position of this poorly characterized parasite lineage.

papers.title: An Ontology for Workplace Violence: Protocol to Support Cross-Sector Incident Reporting in Public Services.
papers.abstract: Underreporting is a defining problem in the documentation of workplace violence across public services. This is reinforced by inconsistent, often poor incident descriptions and the absence of a clear, shared nomenclature. Without an ontology-backed structure, similar events are recorded differently across settings or remain uncodable and effectively invisible. Moreover, workplace violence (WPV) is typically registered and studied within sector- and even organization-specific categories and local reporting logics rather than through a shared semantic framework, limiting comparability and cumula
papers.summary: This paper describes a protocol for developing an ontology to standardize how workplace violence incidents are reported across different public service sectors. The authors argue that inconsistent terminology and sector-specific reporting practices cause underreporting and make incidents hard to compare or aggregate. The ontology aims to provide a shared semantic framework so similar events are coded consistently across settings.

papers.title: Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. Met-SC contains 7  756  867 reference spectra ass
papers.summary: Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that standardizes deposition of metabolomics data, including project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows. It houses over 7.7 million reference spectra and supports online analysis and disease-focused knowledge mining, addressing the growing need for data storage, reuse, and spectral resource management in metabolomics.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that combines network-based disease module identification with drug repurposing prediction, letting users coordinate specialized agents through natural language. It aims to integrate fragmented tools and heterogeneous data sources into a single workflow, addressing the need for cross-disciplinary collaboration in in silico repurposing.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, achieving extensive coverage of UniProtKB and linking to major resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for protein function annotation across biology.

papers.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
papers.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. Cytotoxicity was assessed
papers.summary: This study exposed human macrophage-like THP-1 cells to crystalline silica particles and profiled changes in microRNA expression both inside cells and released extracellularly. The work identifies miRNA signatures associated with silica exposure, proposing these as potential biomarkers for monitoring occupational exposure linked to silicosis and related lung diseases.

papers.title: Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a critical complication affecting patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with multifaceted symptoms requiring systematic management. Current clinical practices lack structured tools to guide nurses in addressing GVHD-related symptoms across diverse organ systems. This review aims to synthesize evidence on GVHD symptom management to construct a knowledge graph, enhancing nursing interventions and improving patient outcomes.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on managing graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) symptoms after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to build a structured knowledge graph for nursing care. The goal is to give nurses a systematic tool for addressing GVHD symptoms across multiple organ systems, where current practice lacks structured guidance.

papers.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. Both strains triggered rapid ET release from neutrophils and T helper 17 cells. However, whereas neutrophil ETs displayed a conserved proteomic profile regardless of the strain, TETs
papers.summary: This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes trigger rapid extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps induced by the two strains showed distinct proteomic programs, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in acne pathogenesis.

papers.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
papers.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reconceived not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. Under this reframing, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs that feed it. The paper is a conceptual/opinion piece rather than a technical or empirical study.

papers.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
papers.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFT
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to Protein Data Bank structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the original SIFTS pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast sequence search, a better scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and refinement based on backbone connectivity. This makes high-quality structure-function mapping accessible to any lab without relying on internal PDBe infrastructure.

papers.title: EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.
papers.abstract: Functional enrichment of transcriptomic datasets can be constrained by incomplete annotation, uneven identifier recognition, and uncertainty about which organism annotation resource provides the most informative functional context. EchoGO is a reproducible downstream framework that retains target GOseq enrichment as the primary functional evidence while evaluating the same transcriptomic response across researcher-selected organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. Evidence is assembled at the GO-term level with its analytical and organism provenance, allowing research
papers.summary: EchoGO is a reproducible framework for functional enrichment of transcriptomic data that keeps GOseq as the primary evidence but evaluates the same gene response across multiple researcher-selected organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. Results are assembled at the GO-term level with analytical and organism provenance, helping address incomplete annotation and uneven identifier recognition.

papers.title: MAOMAO: an ontology-guided FAIR resource for harmonized peptide toxicity data.
papers.summary: MAOMAO is a new ontology-guided resource that harmonizes peptide toxicity data from diverse sources into a FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) framework. It uses ontologies to standardize annotations, enabling consistent comparison and integration of peptide toxicity information. This resource supports drug discovery and safety assessment by making peptide toxicity data more accessible and interoperable.

papers.title: Implementing the ILAE 2025 seizure taxonomy in medical software.
papers.abstract: The International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE), working via a multidisciplinary task force, has issued a position paper with updated seizure classification guidelines (2025) replacing its previous guidance (2017), establishing a revised de-facto standard for clinical assessment and classification of epileptic seizures. The 2025 model simplifies the system, making it easier to adopt in different clinical settings while also clarifying the taxonomic rules, the definition of consciousness, and the application of phenomena-based descriptors. As a result, clinical practitioners, technologists, an
papers.summary: The paper describes how to implement the ILAE 2025 seizure classification guidelines in medical software, replacing the 2017 version. The new taxonomy simplifies seizure classification, clarifies taxonomic rules and the definition of consciousness, and standardizes phenomena-based descriptors for easier clinical adoption. The authors outline software implementation considerations to support consistent clinical assessment and classification of epileptic seizures.

papers.title: HuRInterDB: A Database Exploring the Landscape of lncRNA-Protein Interactions.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) possess diverse biological functions and play key regulatory roles in biological processes by interacting with other biomolecules, such as proteins, RNAs, and the genome. High-throughput RNA-interaction experiments have generated large volumes of lncRNA-protein interaction records. The fragmented deposition of these records across disparate public databases complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. Here, we present HuRInterDB (Human lncRNA-Protein Interaction Database), a comprehensive and standardized database that focuses on human lncRNA-protein in
papers.summary: HuRInterDB is a new standardized database that consolidates human lncRNA-protein interaction records scattered across multiple public sources into a single unified resource. It aims to simplify retrieval and enable integrative analysis of these interactions, which are important for understanding lncRNA regulatory functions.

papers.title: Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health.
papers.abstract: Nutrition science has traditionally focused on dietary intake, nutrient metabolism, physiology, and health outcomes. Although these domains remain fundamental, advancing public health increasingly requires understanding nutrition within the broader systems that shape food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. This Perspective proposes sustainable nutrition as a unifying concept: maintaining nutritional status that supports growth, development, and health across the lifespan while accounting for population needs, context, and the capacity and resilience
papers.summary: This perspective proposes "sustainable nutrition" as a unifying framework that links dietary intake and health outcomes with food production, processing, access, and environmental sustainability. It argues that advancing public health requires understanding nutrition within these broader food-system and environmental contexts rather than focusing on intake and metabolism alone. The paper is conceptual and calls for integrating food systems science, environmental science, and diet research to support both public and planetary health.

papers.title: Integrating cure and care in Alzheimer's disease: a systems perspective for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease remains a major global health challenge, with limited disease-modifying therapies and a rapidly growing societal burden. Although amyloid and tau remain central to the field, current evidence also implicates neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions in disease pathogenesis. These developments support a broader systems framework, but simply combining additional disciplines or data modalities does not by itself preserve the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease. Artificial intelligence multi-omics, and digital biomar
papers.summary: This perspective argues that Alzheimer's disease research should move beyond amyloid and tau to a systems framework incorporating neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions. The authors contend that simply combining more disciplines or data modalities is insufficient; instead, AI-driven multi-omics and digital biomarkers must be integrated in ways that preserve the dynamic biology and lived experience of disease to enable precision medicine.
